content:
Currently we have references listed per module but I was thinking it might be nice to have a master list of at least commonly used references. I think this could serve a few purposes:

  1. Collect physics references that are useful for formalization
  2. Personally I would like to learn more about physics even outside of formalization and having a list of good references from different domains would be great to have for learning more - and I assume some other people may feel the same
  3. If we also list which parts have been formalized (e.g. chapters of a textbook) a nice entry point for new contributes would be to formalize other sections so they have a provided reference that will be practical for formalization

Perhaps this info could be automatically added to the website by compiling the reference lists? Though this would likely require some work to unify the reference style

I think this is a great idea, point 2 is something even I would have a personal interest in. Maybe we could add this as a part to the new API map part of the website that @Alex Zughaid has set up? Almost like a web/map of references only

Likewise, I think this is a great idea. I think we should aim to unify the reference style, as I think this has other benefits as well.

If we find the right reference style, maybe a Linter can help enforce it.

We can extract this information in the future and add it to the website. I've also added check_references.py to check that the ##References section is formatted correctly.

Yeah that’s what I had in mind
Awesome I think it looks good to go! If any changes arise I think it should be informed by the website

My suggestions:

  1. Can we exempt Zulip links from the bibliography? I think it's going to end up cluttering the bibliography and having it in the references isn't particularly helpful when it's just a link.
  2. Can we keep some formatting in the references section? It's helpful to clarify which references are helpful to which concepts.

As an example of 2, the reference for Physlib/ClassicalMechanics/DampedHarmonicOscillator/Basic.lean was

References for the damped harmonic oscillator include:
- Landau & Lifshitz, Mechanics, page 76, section 25.
- Goldstein, Classical Mechanics, Chapter 2.

References for the Caldirola–Kanai lagrangian include:
- Caldirola, Nuovo Cimento 18 (1941) 393.
- Kanai, Progress of Theoretical Physics 3 (1948) 440.

and became 

* Landau & Lifshitz, Mechanics, page 76, section 25. [ref: landau_mechanics]
* Goldstein, Classical Mechanics, Chapter 2. [ref: goldstein_classicalmechanics]
* Caldirola, Nuovo Cimento 18 (1941) 393. [ref: caldirola_1941]
* Kanai, Progress of Theoretical Physics 3 (1948) 440. [ref: kanai_1948]

while I think keeping the subheadings for damped harmonic oscillator and the lagrangian is useful.
